title: Observability with OpenTelemetry: Logs, Traces, Metrics & SLO Alerts
concept: See what production is doing and alert on what users feel: structured logs with trace ids, W3C trace context across services and queues, spans that add up, percentiles from histograms, metric labels that don't explode, and SLO burn-rate alerts instead of noisy thresholds.
description: An advanced course for developers who are paged for their services. Every lesson starts from an incident on the CodeDev learning platform - 800 ms missing from a trace of the submit endpoint, a metrics bill that tripled after someone labelled a counter with user_id, logs that could not be joined to the request that failed, an alert that woke the team 14 times in a week for nothing - and fixes it with instrumentation you can test: logs, metrics and traces, structured logging, trace context and propagation through async code and queues, the Find the Missing 800 ms scenario, histograms and percentiles, cardinality, SLOs and multi-window burn-rate alerts. 12 lessons with True/False quizzes on real traces, logs and dashboards, and TypeScript challenges graded by hidden tests.

learningOutcomes.text: Choose between logs, metrics and traces and write structured logs that join to traces
Propagate W3C trace context across services, async callbacks and queues
Compute percentiles from histograms and read latency honestly
Keep metric labels bounded so cost and queries stay under control
Alert on SLO burn rate over multiple windows instead of instant thresholds

testedVersions.OpenTelemetry JS: lesson examples, check current SDK versions

knownIssues: No collector or backend in the code runner: challenges work on recorded spans, logs and histograms
